questions.question: Which famous Indian musician played shehnai and received Bharat Ratna in the year 2001?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ustad Bismillah Khan__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan was born on 21 March 1916 in Dumraon village, Bihar.
 
• He settled in Varanasi with his father Prophet Bakhsh Khan at a very young age.
 
• Bismillah Khan was awarded the "Bharat Ratna" in 2001 by the Government of India.
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan played the clarinet from the Red Fort when the country became independent in 1947.
 
• He died on 21 August 2006 at the age of 90.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Pandit Ravi Shankar**, mentioned in option 1, was a** sitar player and composer who also received Bharat Ratna in 1999** for his contribution to Indian classical music.
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma,** mentioned in option 2, is a **santoor player who received Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan** awards for his contribution to Indian classical music.
 
• ** Ustad Zakir Hussain**, mentioned in option 3, is **a tabla player who received Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan** awards for his contribution to Indian classical music.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated when the annual harvest takes place in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magh Bihu. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The most important festival of Assam is Bihu. Bihu is a series of three agricultural festivals celebrated with great enthusiasm and fervor throughout the state. These three Bihus are:

 
 
• Rongali Bihu (Bohag Bihu): It is the most popular and widely celebrated Bihu, which marks the arrival of the Assamese New Year in mid-April. It celebrates the onset of the spring season and the agricultural cycle. People indulge in traditional music, dance (Bihu dance), feasting, and various cultural activities.
 
• Kongali Bihu (Kati Bihu): Celebrated in mid-October, Kongali Bihu is dedicated to the worship of the household deities. This Bihu is more somber in nature and focuses on prayers and rituals for a bountiful harvest. People light oil lamps, offer prayers, and participate in community activities.
 
• Bhogali Bihu (Magh Bihu): Celebrated in mid-January, Bhogali Bihu is associated with the harvest and feasting. It is also known as the festival of food, where people enjoy various traditional delicacies, especially made from rice and sesame seeds. Bonfires are lit, and community feasts are organized during this Bihu.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Makaravilakku** is a festival celebrated in Kerala, which marks the end of the Sabarimala pilgrimage season. It falls in January.
 
• **Lohri** is a festival celebrated in Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi, which marks the winter solstice. It falls in January.
 
• **Ponga**l is a harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, which falls in mid-January and is dedicated to the Sun God.

questions.question: The music of Bharatanatyam belongs to ______ of southern India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Carnatic system.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The music of Bharatanatyam belongs to the Carnatic system of southern India.**
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two **main subgenres of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.**
 
• Carnatic music is primarily practiced in the southern Indian states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka.
 
• The music of Bharatanatyam is an integral part of the dance form and is used to express various emotions and moods.
 
• The folk system and Fusion system are not specific to any particular region or dance form, while the Hindustani system is mainly practiced in the northern parts of India.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Folk system** refers to the traditional music of a particular region or community, which is passed down through generations.
 
• ** A fusion system** is a blend of different genres of music, such as classical, jazz, and rock, to create a new sound.
 
• ** Hindustani music** is mainly practiced in the northern parts of India, including states like Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra. It is characterized by its use of ragas and talas and is often accompanied by the sitar or the tabla.

questions.question: Which disease is caused by the deficiency of protein in the diet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Kwashiorkor.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Kwashiorkor disease of caused by protein deficiency.
 
• Kwashiorkor, also known as “edematous malnutrition” because of its association with edema (fluid retention), is a nutritional disorder most often seen in regions experiencing famine.
 
• It is a form of malnutrition caused by a lack of protein in the diet. People who have kwashiorkor typically have an extremely emaciated appearance in all body parts except their ankles, feet, and belly, which swell with fluid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which state was ranked first in the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) Awards 2021?
questions.solution:

• **The correct answer is option 1, Uttar Pradesh, which was ranked first in the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) Awards 2021. **
 
• ** PMAY-U is a flagship housing scheme launched by the Government of India in 2015 with the aim of providing affordable housing to the urban poor. The scheme targets the economically weaker sections (EWS), low-income groups (LIG), and middle-income groups (MIG) in urban areas.**
 
• The PMAY-U Awards are given to states, cities, and beneficiaries for their outstanding performance in implementing the scheme and achieving its objectives. The awards were announced on 25th June 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
 
• Uttar Pradesh was ranked first in the category of Best Performing State in the implementation of PMAY-U, with a score of 85.50 out of 100. The state was recognized for its efforts in completing the construction of houses within the stipulated time frame and ensuring quality and affordability of the houses.
 
• Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana were also among the top-performing states in the PMAY-U Awards 2021. Kerala was ranked second, Tamil Nadu was ranked third, and Haryana was ranked fourth. These states were appreciated for their innovative approaches, use of technology, and community participation in the implementation of the schemeh.

questions.question: Which Lodi ruler's (1489 AD-1517 AD) real name was Nizam Khan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikandar Lod**__i.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original name of the Sikandar Lodi was Nizam Khan__.
 
• Sikandar Lodi (1489 to 1517) was a ruler of the Lodhi dynasty.
 
• He established Agra city in 1504.
 
• He shifted his capital from Delhi to Agra in 1506.
 
• Jauna khan was the childhood name of Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.
 
• Farid was the childhood name of Shershah Suri. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikandar Lodi** was the son of Bahlul Lodi, the **founder of the Lodi dynasty.**

 
 
• He ruled from 1489 AD to 1517 AD and was known for his military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms.
 
• Sikandar Lodi was succeeded by his son, Ibrahim Lodi, who was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Panipat in 1526 AD, leading to the end of the Lodi dynasty and the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
 
 
• **Qutbuddin Mubarak **Shah was a ruler of the Slave dynasty in India, who ruled from 1316 AD to 1320 AD.
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last ruler of the Lodi dynasty before it was overthrown by Babur. Bahlul Lodi was the founder of the Lodi dynasty and the father of Sikandar Lodi.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the fundamental duty "sovereignty, unity and integrity of India" is mentioned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A (c).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

 
• Fundamental Duties:

 
 
• The fundamental duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of our constitution through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• At present, there are eleven fundamental duties under article 51 A of the constitution.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties has been borrowed from the erstwhile USSR.
 
• Originally the duties were ten in number, later on through 86th Amendment Act, 2002, the eleventh Fundamental duty was added.
 
• Swaran Singh Committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-enforceable in nature.
 
• Following are the eleven Fundamental Duties:
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity, so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six to fourteen years. This duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

questions.question: The rock shelters of Bhimbetka are in the foothills of which mountains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Vindhya Range__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka is located in the Raisen District of Madhya Pradesh.

 
 
• It is located near Abdullaganj town and inside the Ratapani Wildlife Sanctuary (Southern edge of Vindhya Range).
 
• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ 

 
• Bhimbetka was discovered by archaeologist V S Wakankar in 1957.​

 
 
• It was one of the oldest paintings in India and the world.
 
• The Bhimbetka rock shelters are an archaeological site of the Paleolithic age.
 
• These cave paintings show tremendous similarity to the aboriginal rock paintings of the Savanna regions of Australia, the paintings done by pygmies of the Kalahari Desert, and the Paleolithic Lascaux cave paintings of France.

questions.question:
Which of the following factors can affect distribution of population?

I. Geographical factors

II. Social factors

III. Cultural factors

IV. Economic factors
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II, III and IV.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Geographical factors such as topography, climate, and availability of natural resources can affect the distribution of population.**
 
• **Social factors such as access to healthcare, education, and basic amenities can also play a role in population distribution.**
 
• ** Cultural factors such as language, religion, and customs can influence where people choose to live.**
 
• ** Economic factors such as job opportunities, income levels, and cost of living can also impact population distribution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Geographical factors:** This refers to physical features of the land such as mountains, rivers, and coastlines. These factors can affect the availability of resources and the ease of transportation, which can impact where people choose to live. Social factors: This includes access to healthcare, education, and basic amenities such as clean water and sanitation. These factors can impact quality of life and make certain areas more attractive to live in.
 
• **Cultural factors**: This refers to shared beliefs, values, and customs that can influence where people choose to live and how they interact with others.
 
• **Economic factors**: This includes job opportunities, income levels, and cost of living. These factors can affect a person's ability to afford housing and other basic needs, which can impact where they choose to live.

questions.question: In 1900, India participated in Olympics games which was held in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Paris.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **The correct answer is option 1, Paris. India participated in the 1900 Olympics which were held in Paris, France.**
 
• The 1900 Olympics were the second modern Olympics and were held from May 14 to October 28, 1900.
 
• India made its debut in the Olympics in the 1900 Paris Olympics and was represented by a single athlete, Norman Pritchard. He won two silver medals in athletics events.
 
• The Olympics in 1900 were a part of the Paris World Fair and were spread over several months. The events were not well organized, and many of the athletes did not even realize that they were competing in the Olympics.
 
• The other options mentioned in the question are incorrect. Athens, Greece, hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896, Berlin, Germany, hosted the Olympics in 1936, and Tokyo, Japan, hosted the Olympics in 1964 and will host again in 2021.

questions.question: Bhagat Singh was executed on March 23, 1931 along with ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sukhdev and Rajguru.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On March 23, 1931, Bhagat Singh along with his associates Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru were hanged to death for the assassination of 21-year-old British police officer John Saunders.
 
• The day Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru lay down their lives for Freedom is called Martyrs' Day.
 
• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were hanged to death 11 hours before the scheduled time for Saunder's murder case.
 
• They mistook Saunders for Superintendent James Scott, who was responsible for leading a lathi charge against Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai was protesting against the Simon Commission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The famous slogan ‘Inquilab Zindabad’ was popularized by Bhagat Singh.
 
• Bhagat Singh was sentenced to death for the Lahore conspiracy case.
 
• On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh, along with freedom fighter Batukeshwar Dutt, hurled two bombs inside the Central Legislative Assembly in New Delhi to protest against an unfavorable Bill.

questions.question: Which among the following gases is used in the artificial ripening of fruits?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Acetylene__.

__
 
• Acetylene gas liberated from calcium carbide is some of the commercial ripening agents used successfully in the trade.
 
• They have been widely studied for their effectiveness in initiating and accelerating the ripening process and their effect on fruit quality and health-related issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39997ab25e68a0037d9b6e6fc32720c9844f92b075aa45bd0314bdc2cbc8713d.png] Mistake Point__

__
 
• Ethylene is used in the natural ripening process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__Artificial ripening:

 
• ​It is done to achieve faster and more uniform ripening characteristics.
 
• In general is a physiological process that makes the fruit edible, palatable, and nutritious.
 
• Usually, fruits produce ethylene gas, a plant hormone, naturally, that ripens the fruits.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain range is the oldest in India?

questions.question: The blood platelets are also known as ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __Thrombocytes.____ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__Blood Platelets

__
 
• Platelets also called thrombocytes, are cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes (special cells in the bone marrow).
 
• Blood normally contains 200,000-300,000 platelets mm Cubic.
 
• Platelets can release a variety of substances most of which are involved in the coagulation or clotting of blood.
 
• A reduction in their number can lead to clotting disorders which will lead to excessive loss of blood from the body.
 
• Blood is a special connective tissue consisting of a fluid matrix, plasma, and formed elements
 
• Plasma is a straw-coloured, viscous fluid constituting nearly 55 per cent of the blood. 90-92 per cent of plasma is water and proteins contribute 6-8 per cent of it.
 
• Fibrinogen, globulins and albumins are the major proteins
 
• Erythrocytes, leukocytes, and platelets are collectively called formed elements and they constitute nearly 45 per cent of the blood

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ 

 
• Erythrocytes or red blood cells (RBC) are the most abundant of all the cells in the blood. A healthy adult man has, on average, 5 million to 5.5 million RBCs mm–3 of blood. 
 
• Leucocytes are also known as white blood cells (WBC) as they are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin. They are nucleated and are relatively lesser in number which averages 6000-8000 mm3 of blood.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of 'River of Smoke' novel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Amitav Ghosh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **River of Smokes is a novel written by Amitav Ghosh, an Indian writer who is known for his fiction work.**
 
• River of Smokes is the second volume in the trilogy preceded by Sea of Poppies and followed by Flood of Fire.
 
• In December 2018, Amitav Ghosh became the first Indian writer in English to receive the Jnanpith Award. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/292e0c96dd6c006ce1f3ef21b86308c7c73a2bc69f508d641b46f352d114f429.png] Important Points__

 
• Renowned English fiction writer Amitav Ghosh has been selected for the Jnanpith award, 2018.
 
• This has been announced by Jnanpith Selection Board on 14 December 2018.
 
• Amitav Ghosh was born in Calcutta in 1956.
 
• He is an alumnus of Doon School, Dehradun, St. Stephen’s College, Delhi University and Delhi School of Economics.
 
• He was awarded Padma Shri in 2007 and was elected as Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in 2009.
 
• He was also named Ford Foundation Art of Change Fellow in 2015.

His works :

 
• The Circle of Reason (1986) was his first novel.
 
• Other fiction works include The Shadow Lines (1988), The Calcutta Chromosome (1995), The Glass Palace (2000), The Hungry Tide (2004).
 
• He has also written three works as a part of The Ibis trilogy of which the first volume is Sea of Poppies (2008); the second volume is River of Smoke (2011), and the third volume is Flood of Fire (2015).
 
• His notable non-fiction works include Antique Land (1992), Dancing in Cambodia and at Large in Burma (1998), Countdown (1999), and The Imam and the Indian (2002), The Great Derangement: Climate Change and the Unthinkable (2016).
